title: AI Platform Agents: control at the boundary
lede: Discovery and control for agents running inside third-party AI platforms — hosted copilots, managed agent runtimes. Identity and runtime belong to the platform, not your infrastructure; you control what those agents do when they cross into your estate.

nodes.label: Discover + bring under policy
sub: same policy model as everything else

nodes.label: Acting for a user
sub: CIAM-adjacent: user context rides on the call

edges.label: on behalf of an end user

steps.title: Platform agents emit activity
steps.what: Hosted copilots and managed agent runtimes emit agent activity that Privilege can discover — the workloads themselves live outside your control.

steps.title: One policy model for all of it
steps.what: Discovered platform agents are brought under the same policy model as everything else, so control does not fork between agent origins.

steps.title: Control at the crossing point
steps.what: What a platform-hosted agent may reach when it crosses into your estate — tools, data, models — is gated through the AI Gateway.

steps.title: The user-boundary caveat
steps.what: These are employee-facing platform agents, so this is a workforce story. The CIAM-adjacent concern is only at the boundary: what a platform agent may access on behalf of a user, which flows as user context on the call.
